# Why Do I Keep Watching Porn Even Though I Don’t Like It?


Why do I keep watching porn even when I don’t enjoy it?


If you’re asking, “why do I keep watching porn,” habits and emotional triggers may help explain the pattern. Have you ever found yourself visiting a porn site even though you were not particularly interested in watching it? You might have told yourself that you were going to stop or you knew it was likely to leave you feeling disappointed. However, you ended up scrolling through.


Once finished you might be left wondering;


Why did I do that?! I didn’t even like it!


This can be confusing. It can make you think that you like watching it because you are doing it. However, we often get sucked into certain habits due to our emotions.


For some people, watching[pornography](https://blockerx.net/blog/how-to-quit-watching-porn-top-7-tips/) becomes a way to cope with boredom, stress, loneliness or uncomfortable feelings. This can therefore make us continue to watch.


Understanding why you are continuing to watch pornography when you don’t like it will help you understand what is causing the urge and help you make changes.


## Why Do I Keep Watching Porn Even Though I Don’t Like It?


One common answer to “why do I keep watching porn” is that the behaviour has become a habit. You could be watching pornography due to habit.


As we repeat certain actions in the same situation, it can become a habit. We often feel like we just have to do it without thinking.


For example, if you often watch pornography before bed. Initially you might have liked watching it. However, after doing it many times you might start to associate going to bed with watching pornography.


Even though you aren’t very interested, you will continue to do it due to habit.


This can create a cycle;


Trigger – You feel bored, stressed, lonely.


Impulse – You feel an urge to watch pornography.


Action – You visit a site.


Temporary reward – You feel stimulated/ distracted.


After – You feel disappointed/ unsatisfied. However, you have formed a habit.


You are likely doing it due to association and not because you are intentionally doing it.


## 7 Reasons Why You’re Watching Porn Even Though You Don’t Like It


There could be many reasons as to why you are watching pornography even though it isn’t satisfying. Below are some common reasons.


### 1. It’s Become a Habit


When do you usually watch pornography? Late at night? When you wake up? During breaks at work? When you have some free time?


If you are continually watching pornography at the same times, it can become a habit.


For example, when you get home you might start scrolling on your[phone](https://blockerx.net/blog/how-to-stop-watching-porn-at-night/) and automatically visit a pornography site. This might not be intentional but has become a habit.


This can be why you are watching even though you aren’t very aroused or interested.


Start by identifying when and where you usually watch. Once you understand why you are doing it you can start to make changes.


### 2. You’re Distracting Yourself From Uncomfortable Feelings


Another answer to “why do I keep watching porn” may be emotional avoidance rather than sexual interest. At times pornography can be a way to distract yourself from uncomfortable feelings.


You might be feeling lonely, stressed about work, anxious, frustrated, bored or disappointed.


Therefore, you might be watching it less for the sexual aspect and more for the temporary distraction.


For example, if you’ve had a bad day at work and feel stressed. You might visit a pornography site. This takes your mind off your worries.


However, once you stop watching you will still feel the same.


If this is happening regularly, you might start to associate pornography with feeling better. Therefore, you might automatically look for distractions.


Ask yourself why you are really watching it.


### 3. It Doesn’t Excite You Anymore


Have you noticed that you don’t get as excited watching pornography?


You might be taking longer to scroll through, switching between videos or searching for something to catch your eye. Once you finish you might feel like you didn’t really get much out of it.


This might be because your expectations have changed and you are looking for the same excitement.


However, it doesn’t necessarily mean that you are becoming desensitised or addicted.


Often our sexual interest and satisfaction can depend on our stress levels, sleep, mood, personal circumstances and expectations.


However, if you are constantly searching for something and not enjoying it then you might be struggling to control your behaviour.


### 4. Certain Triggers Are Causing You To Watch


This can help explain why do I keep watching porn at particular times or in particular situations. A trigger is something you feel, something that is happening or something in your environment that makes you more likely to engage in a certain behaviour.


Triggers for pornography could be;


Being alone in your bedroom


Scrolling through suggestive content on social media.


Staying up late.


Taking your phone into the bathroom.


Feeling bored during the day.


Feeling stressed/frustrated.


If you often watch pornography when you are alone at night your brain will start to associate this with watching pornography.


Eventually you will feel the urge to watch when you are alone at night. Even though you don’t really want to.


Whilst you may not be able to avoid all triggers, you can avoid situations that cause you to do this regularly.


### 5. You’re Using It As A Quick Fix


For some people asking “why do I keep watching porn,” the search is really for a quick change in mood. Sometimes we watch pornography because we want a quick change in our mood.


Pornography is easily accessible. You can open a site in seconds with no planning.


If you’re feeling bored, restless or your brain is tired it can be an easy way to get some stimulation or distraction.


However, this won’t really provide you with any satisfaction.


You might feel an urge, watch pornography and then feel a quick change in mood. However, you’ll feel the same frustration/boredom/stress.


Ask yourself;


What am I really looking for?


You might realise you actually need some rest, socialisation, exercise or a break from a stressful situation.


### 6. You’re Getting Tired Of Trying To Stop


If you keep asking yourself “why do I keep watching porn” after deciding to stop, repeated habit patterns may be involved. Trying to stop watching pornography and constantly falling back into the habit can be exhausting.


You might have told yourself you’re going to stop many times. However, a few days later you’re back into the same routine.


This can impact your confidence. You might start to think you’ll never be able to stop or that there is no point in trying.


Don’t see this as a reason you can’t change. Instead look at why this is happening. Were you feeling a certain way? Were you alone? Did you stay up late with your phone?


Understanding your patterns will give you something to work on.


### 7. You’re In A Habit Loop


A habit loop is a great way to understand why we get into habits.


Generally a habit loop consists of;


Cue – Something that makes you want to engage in the behaviour. This could be feeling bored, stressed, lonely or a certain time of day.


Routine – You open a pornography site and watch sexual content.


Reward – You feel temporarily stimulated/distraction.


The reward doesn’t need to be very satisfying. It can just be a quick change in your mood.


If this becomes a regular occurrence you’ll start to automatically feel the urge.


The key is to learn to recognise the cues and change your routine.


## When Does Watching Porn Become A Problem?


Watching pornography doesn’t necessarily mean you’re addicted or suffering from a mental health issue. However, if you notice some of the below you might want to seek some help;


You’re constantly trying to cut down or stop but struggling.


You’re spending a lot more time than intended.


Neglecting work/studies/sleep/relationships/personal responsibilities.


Continuing to watch despite negative consequences.


Using pornography regularly to cope with uncomfortable feelings.


Continuing to engage with pornography despite not really getting any satisfaction.


[Compulsive Sexual Behaviour Disorder](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5775124/) (CSBD) is recognised in the[World Health Organisation’s](https://iris.who.int/bitstream/handle/10665/375767/9789240077263-eng.pdf) (ICD-11). It is an impulse control disorder. It involves a persistent pattern of difficulty controlling intense and repetitive sexual impulses/urges which leads to repetitive sexual behaviour.


However, not everyone who watches pornography frequently has CSBD. If you’re only feeling distressed due to moral judgements then this isn’t enough to diagnose.


If you’re concerned about your behaviour a qualified mental health professional can help you.


## 8 Ways To Stop Watching Porn When You Don’t Like It


If you’re struggling to stop watching pornography you might not want to rely on your will power.


Instead, try to understand what is causing you to watch it, change your situations and create healthier routines.


### 1. Understand Your Triggers


When asking “why do I keep watching porn,” start by noticing when the urge appears. Start by noticing when you feel the urge to watch.


Are you feeling the urge late at night? Do you watch when you feel lonely? Are you using it to avoid work? Do you watch when you’re feeling stressed? Are you being triggered by certain apps/sites?


Write this down in a notebook or on your phone.


Try to notice any patterns without judging yourself. Once you know what is causing you to watch you can plan healthier alternatives.


### 2. Change Your Routines


If you often watch pornography in the same place/at the same time try to change this.


For example, if you are often watching whilst in bed try charging your phone elsewhere. If you often watch when you’re very bored try to plan something to do.


Making small changes to your environment can help prevent you doing something you’re used to.


### 3. Limit Access To Porn Sites


If pornography is easily accessible it can be harder to stop yourself doing it on impulse.


Try limiting;


Removing any saved links/bookmarks.


Uninstalling apps that are triggering you.


Turning off any unnecessary notifications.


Blocking sites using[website blockers](https://blockerx.net/blog/how-to-quit-porn-in-15-steps/) .


Keeping your phone out of your bedroom.


Using tools like BlockerX can help you limit your access to unwanted sites.


Website blockers shouldn’t be used as a replacement for addressing any emotional/behavioural issues but can help you set boundaries for yourself.


### 4. Create An Alternative Routine


If pornography has become part of your daily routine decide what you’re going to do instead.


Try something easy;


Go for a short walk.


Exercise/stretch.


Read a book.


Call a friend.


Listen to music.


Cook.


Do a hobby.


Complete a small task.


Choose something that fits with your lifestyle. This will help you create a routine that will help your wellbeing.


### 5. Practice Saying No To The Urge


You might feel like the urge is overwhelming but this doesn’t mean you have to give in.


Next time you feel the urge try waiting 10 minutes before making a decision. Put your phone down, leave the room or go for a short walk.


Try to take some deep breaths or practice mindfulness.


Try to notice what you’re feeling without judging yourself. The urge might fade or you might still feel it. Either way you can practice making a choice.


The aim isn’t to stop having sexual thoughts but to give yourself more control.


### 6. Improve Your Sleep And Routine


If your routine is quite lax you might be creating more opportunities for unwanted habits.


If you often stay up late with your phone it can be easier to fall back into pornography.


Try to go to bed at the same time each night. Keep your phone out of your bedroom and do something relaxing before bed.


Make sure you’re doing some exercise, work, hobbies and socialising during the day.


### 7. Don’t Feel Shame


If you’re trying to stop watching pornography you might experience setbacks.


Instead of feeling like you’ve lost all progress try to understand why this happened.


What were you feeling? What caused you to watch? Were you tired/stressed/lonely? What can you change next time?


Use your answers to improve your plan. Focus on understanding your behaviour and making changes.


### 8. Seek Professional Help


If you’re struggling to control your pornography use and it is impacting your relationships, work, studies, sleep or emotional wellbeing then seek help from a qualified mental health professional.


Psychological therapies such as[Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40126561/) and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) have been studied for problematic pornography use.


A therapist can help you understand your triggers, address any underlying issues and create a plan to suit your situation.


You don’t have to wait until it becomes a big problem.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Why Do I Keep Watching Porn Even Though I’m Not Horny?


You might not be watching pornography due to sexual desires. It could have become a habit due to feeling bored, lonely, stressed or a certain time of day. You might be doing it due to a routine.


### Why Don’t I Enjoy Watching Porn Anymore?


Often our sexual feelings can change. Our stress levels, mood, sleep, expectations and habits can all impact how much we enjoy it. If you’re constantly scrolling without getting much out of it then it might be becoming hard to control.


### Can You Become Addicted To Something You Don’t Like?


We often continue to do things even if we’re not enjoying them. This can be due to forming habits, struggling to control our impulses and continuing despite negative consequences. However, just because you don’t like it doesn’t mean you’re addicted.


### Is Watching Porn Every Day An Addiction?


Not necessarily. It’s more important to consider if you’re struggling to control the behaviour, constantly failing to cut down, having significant negative consequences and impacting your daily life.


### Why Do I Regret Watching Porn?


You might be feeling disappointed because it doesn’t align with your goals and boundaries. You might also be frustrated that you’ve wasted your time. Instead of constantly blaming yourself try to understand why you did it.


### How Do I Stop Watching Porn Due To Boredom?


Identify when you usually feel bored and plan something to do. Try going for a walk, exercising, reading, calling someone or doing a hobby. Limit easy access to triggering sites.


### How Long Does It Take To Break A Porn Habit?


There isn’t really a set amount of time. It depends on how much of a habit it is, your triggers, your situation and the changes you make. Focus on making consistent changes.


## Final Thoughts


It can be frustrating when you continue to watch pornography even though you don’t like it. You might feel like you’re going against your own decisions. Especially if you’ve told yourself you’re going to stop multiple times.


However, it might not be because you’re enjoying it. It could be due to automatic routines, emotional triggers, temporary relief or it becoming hard to stop.


Instead of asking yourself why you’re doing it try to understand what is happening before.


Notice your triggers, change your situations, create healthier routines and practice saying no.


If you’re struggling to control your behaviour and it is impacting important areas of your life then seek help.


You are not defined by a habit you’re trying to change. Understanding your pattern is a meaningful first step in creating a healthier relationship with pornography and your digital habits.
